issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree charging colliery machinery does not require registration where the machinery has not been shown to be permanently embedded in the earth.
material_facts: An execution proceeding sought enforcement of a compromise decree that charged listed machinery at a colliery as security for payment.
The judgment debtor objected that the decree included properties outside the suit and was unregistered, and therefore could not be executed.
The High Court found from the decree that the machinery was movable property.
The judgment debtor did not establish that the machinery had been permanently embedded in the earth.
issues.conclusion: The decree did not require registration on the basis asserted, and the judgment debtor failed to establish that it was invalid or unexecutable for want of registration.
issues.legal_principle: The machinery could not be treated as immovable property without establishing that it was permanently embedded in the earth. Since the machinery was found to be movable, registration was not required on the ground advanced. The judgment debtor bore the burden of establishing the asserted invalidity. The judgment refers to no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

predicates.execution_proceeding_for_compromise_decr: The proceeding sought execution of a decree recording a compromise.
predicates.decree_charges_machinery_as_security: The decree charged machinery as security for payment of the amount due.
predicates.debtor_proved_permanent_embedding: The judgment debtor established that the charged machinery was permanently embedded in the earth.

issues.definition: When execution is sought of a compromise decree charging machinery as security and the judgment debtor has not established that the machinery is permanently embedded, the decree is executable without registration.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may decline to consider new pleas that were not raised in the lower courts and do not present pure questions of law.
material_facts: During the appeal, the judgment debtor sought to advance pleas that had not been raised before either the executing court or the High Court.
The proposed pleas did not raise pure questions of law.
issues.conclusion: The court declined to allow the judgment debtor to advance the new pleas.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to consider pleas not raised in the lower courts where those pleas did not raise pure questions of law. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_from_execution_proceeding: The matter before the court was an appeal arising from an execution proceeding.
predicates.plea_not_raised_in_lower_courts: The party had not advanced the plea before the lower courts.
predicates.plea_not_pure_question_of_law: The plea required consideration beyond a pure question of law.

issues.definition: In an appeal arising from execution, a plea not raised in the lower courts and not presenting a pure question of law is not considered on appeal.
